precepts.text: Hezekiah made a pool and a conduit and brought water into the city, the water system he now used against the siege.
precepts.point: He sets captains over the people and comforts them: be strong and courageous, for there be more with us than with him; with him is an arm of flesh, but with us is the Lord our God to help us and fight our battles.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 32: Assyria Defeated and Hezekiah's End

precepts.why:
Kings records “the rest of the acts of Hezekiah, and all his might, and how he made a pool, and a conduit, and brought water into the city”. Hezekiah had built a water system for Jerusalem, and now he used it against the siege.

When “Sennacherib king of Assyria came, and entered into Judah, and encamped against the fenced cities”, Hezekiah took counsel “to stop the waters of the fountains which were without the city”, and the people “stopped all the fountains, and the brook that ran through the midst of the land, saying, Why should the kings of Assyria come, and find much water?” The water came into the city, and the enemy outside found none.

He also “built up all the wall that was broken, and raised it up to the towers, and another wall without, and repaired Millo in the city of David, and made darts and shields in abundance.” Our people are resourceful and skilled, doing the work themselves.

precepts.text: Cursed be the man that trusteth in man and maketh flesh his arm, the opposite of Hezekiah's trust in the Most High.
precepts.point: He sets captains over the people and comforts them: be strong and courageous, for there be more with us than with him; with him is an arm of flesh, but with us is the Lord our God to help us and fight our battles.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 32: Assyria Defeated and Hezekiah's End

precepts.why:
“Thus saith the Lord; Cursed be the man that trusteth in man, and maketh flesh his arm, and whose heart departeth from the Lord.” That is the opposite of Hezekiah’s trust in the Most High.

Hezekiah set captains over the people and spake comfortably to them: “Be strong and courageous, be not afraid nor dismayed for the king of Assyria, nor for all the multitude that is with him: for there be more with us than with him: With him is an arm of flesh; but with us is the Lord our God to help us, and to fight our battles.”

Sennacherib made flesh his arm; Hezekiah trusted the Lord. “And the people rested themselves upon the words of Hezekiah king of Judah.”

precepts.text: Beware lest any man spoil you through vain deceit, for the enemy still seeks to deceive Israel out of the truth.
precepts.point: He argues that no god of any nation delivered its people from his hand, so neither will the God of Hezekiah. This is the same seed the world plants to make Israel weary and turn a people off one accord.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 32: Assyria Defeated and Hezekiah's End

precepts.why:
“Beware lest any man spoil you through philosophy and vain deceit, after the tradition of men, after the rudiments of the world, and not after Christ.” The enemy still seeks to deceive Israel out of the truth.

That is what Sennacherib’s servants were doing at the wall of Jerusalem. “Whereon do ye trust, that ye abide in the siege in Jerusalem?” They claimed Hezekiah was persuading the people “to give over yourselves to die by famine and by thirst”. They mocked that he had “taken away his high places and his altars, and commanded Judah and Jerusalem, saying, Ye shall worship before one altar”, twisting obedience to the commandment into a weakness.

Then the argument: “no god of any nation or kingdom was able to deliver his people out of mine hand”, so “how much less shall your God deliver you out of mine hand?” “Now therefore let not Hezekiah deceive you, nor persuade you on this manner, neither yet believe him”. This is the same seed the world plants to make Israel weary and turn a people off one accord.

precepts.text: Isaiah tells Hezekiah to set his house in order for he shall die, and after Hezekiah prays the Lord adds fifteen years to his life and defends the city.
precepts.point: Then Hezekiah humbles himself for the pride of his heart, he and the people of Jerusalem, so that the wrath of the Lord does not come upon them in his days.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 32: Assyria Defeated and Hezekiah's End

precepts.why:
Kings gives the fuller account of the sickness. “In those days was Hezekiah sick unto death.” Isaiah came and said, “Set thine house in order; for thou shalt die, and not live.” Hezekiah “turned his face to the wall, and prayed unto the Lord”, “I beseech thee, O Lord, remember now how I have walked before thee in truth and with a perfect heart”, “And Hezekiah wept sore.”

Before Isaiah was out of the middle court the word came: “I have heard thy prayer, I have seen thy tears: behold, I will heal thee”. “And I will add unto thy days fifteen years; and I will deliver thee and this city out of the hand of the king of Assyria; and I will defend this city for mine own sake, and for my servant David’s sake.”

That is the benefit done to him. And yet “Hezekiah rendered not again according to the benefit done unto him; for his heart was lifted up: therefore there was wrath upon him, and upon Judah and Jerusalem.” When things go well, do not get puffed up and make it about yourself. “Notwithstanding Hezekiah humbled himself for the pride of his heart, both he and the inhabitants of Jerusalem, so that the wrath of the Lord came not upon them in the days of Hezekiah.”

precepts.text: The sign is the shadow returning ten degrees backward on the sundial of Ahaz, a thing only the Most High could do.
precepts.point: Then Hezekiah humbles himself for the pride of his heart, he and the people of Jerusalem, so that the wrath of the Lord does not come upon them in his days.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 32: Assyria Defeated and Hezekiah's End

precepts.why:
Chronicles says only that the Lord “gave him a sign.” Kings shows what it was. Hezekiah asked, “What shall be the sign that the Lord will heal me”? Isaiah answered, “shall the shadow go forward ten degrees, or go back ten degrees?”

Hezekiah said, “It is a light thing for the shadow to go down ten degrees: nay, but let the shadow return backward ten degrees.” “And Isaiah the prophet cried unto the Lord: and he brought the shadow ten degrees backward, by which it had gone down in the dial of Ahaz.” The shadow returning backward on the sundial of Ahaz was a thing only the Most High could do.

That was the benefit Hezekiah was shown, and it is why his lifted-up heart afterward brought wrath, until he humbled himself.
